articles.content_en: Article 1 These Regulations are formulated to promote the healthy development of new-type urbanization, advance the full coverage of basic public services and conveniences for the resident population, protect the legitimate rights and interests of citizens, and promote social fairness and justice.

Article 2 Citizens who leave their permanent residence registration location, reside in another city for more than half a year, and meet one of the conditions of having lawful and stable employment, lawful and stable residence, or continuous schooling, may apply for a residence permit in accordance with the provisions of these Regulations.

Article 3 A residence permit is a certificate for the holder to reside at the place of residence, enjoy basic public services and conveniences as a resident population, and apply for registration of permanent residence.

Article 4 The contents recorded on a residence permit include: name, gender, ethnicity, date of birth, citizen identification number, personal photo, address of permanent residence registration, address of place of residence, issuing authority of the certificate, and date of issuance.

Article 5 People's governments at or above the county level shall establish and improve mechanisms to provide basic public services and conveniences to residence permit holders. The relevant departments of the people's governments at or above the county level, such as development and reform, education, public security, civil affairs, judicial administration, human resources and social security, housing and urban-rural construction, and health and family planning, shall, in accordance with their respective duties, properly carry out the protection of rights and interests, services, and management of residence permit holders.

Article 6 People's governments at or above the county level shall incorporate the work of providing basic public services and conveniences to residence permit holders into the national economic and social development plans, improve the fiscal transfer payment system, and include the expenses required for providing basic public services and conveniences into the fiscal budget.

Article 7 The relevant departments of the people's governments at or above the county level shall establish and improve the population information database, categorize and improve information systems such as labor and employment, education, social security, real estate, credit, health and family planning, and marriage, as well as the collection and registration of residence permit holder information, strengthen the sharing of residence permit holder information among departments and regions, provide information support for advancing the transfer and continuation systems of social insurance and housing provident fund, and achieve full coverage of basic public services for the resident population, and provide conveniences for residence permit holders to reside at their place of residence.

Article 8 The public security organ shall be responsible for the management of residence permit documents, including acceptance of applications, production, issuance, and endorsement.
The residents' committees, villagers' committees, employing units, schools at which the applicant is studying, and house lessors shall assist in properly carrying out the acceptance of applications and issuance of residence permits.

Article 9 To apply for a residence permit, an applicant shall submit to the local public security station or a community service institution authorized by the public security organ his or her resident identity card, personal photo, and certification materials for place of residence, employment, schooling, etc.
Certification of place of residence includes a house lease contract, a house property ownership certificate, a house purchase contract, or accommodation certificates issued by the house lessor, the employing unit, or the school at which the applicant is studying; certification of employment includes a business license, a labor contract, a certificate of labor relationship issued by the employing unit, or other materials that can prove lawful and stable employment; certification of schooling includes a student ID card or other materials issued by the school that can prove continuous schooling.
Minors under the age of 16 and elderly or disabled persons with mobility difficulties may have their guardians or close relatives apply for a residence permit on their behalf. Where guardians or close relatives handle the application on their behalf, they shall provide the legal and valid identity documents of the principal and the agent.
The applicant and the person issuing the relevant certification materials shall be responsible for the truthfulness and legality of the certification materials as provided in this Article.
Where the application materials are incomplete, the public security station or the community service institution authorized by the public security organ shall inform the applicant of the materials to be supplemented at one time.
Where the conditions for residence permit issuance are met, the public security organ shall produce and issue the residence permit within 15 days from the date of acceptance; in remote areas, areas with inconvenient transportation, or due to special circumstances where the residence permit cannot be produced and issued on time, the local people's government at or above the city with districts may, in its implementation measures, extend the time limit for production and issuance, but the extension shall not exceed 30 days at most.

Article 10 A residence permit shall be issued by the public security organ of the people's government at the county level, and shall be endorsed once every year.
Where a residence permit holder continuously resides at the place of residence, he or she shall go through the endorsement procedures at the local public security station or a community service institution authorized by the public security organ within one month before each anniversary of the residence.
Where the endorsement procedures are not handled within the time limit, the functions of the residence permit shall be suspended; where the endorsement procedures are handled retroactively, the functions of the residence permit shall be restored, and the period of residence of the residence permit holder at the place of residence shall be calculated continuously from the date of retroactive handling of the endorsement procedures.

Article 11 Where the residence permit is damaged to an extent that it is illegible or is lost, the holder of the residence permit shall go through the procedures for replacement or reissuance at the local public security police station or the community service agency authorized by the public security organ.
When the holder of the residence permit replaces the permit with a new one, the original permit shall be returned.

Article 14 The relevant departments of the State Council, the local people's governments at all levels and their relevant departments shall actively create conditions, gradually expand the scope of public services and conveniences provided to the holders of the residence permit, improve the service standards, and regularly make public to the society the scope of public services and conveniences enjoyed by the holders of the residence permit.

Article 15 Where the holder of the residence permit meets the conditions for household registration set by the people's government of the place of residence, the holder may, according to his or her own will, transfer the permanent residence registration from the original place of household registration to the place of residence.

Article 16 The people's government of the place of residence shall determine the conditions for household registration according to the following provisions:
(1) The conditions for household registration in an organized town and a small city with an urban population of less than 500,000 are to have a legal and stable residence in the urban area of the city, the town where the people's government of the county is located, or other organized towns.
(2) The conditions for household registration in a medium-sized city with an urban population of 500,000 to 1 million are to have a legal and stable employment and a legal and stable residence in the city, and to have participated in urban social insurance for a certain number of years as prescribed by the State. Among them, for places with low pressure on comprehensive carrying capacity of the city, the restrictions on household registration may be fully liberalized by reference to the standards for organized towns and small cities; for places with high pressure on comprehensive carrying capacity of the city, regulations may be made on the scope and duration of legal and stable employment and the scope and conditions of legal and stable residence, provided that no requirements such as housing area or amount shall be set for the legal and stable residence, and the requirement for the number of years of participation in urban social insurance shall not exceed three years.
(3) The conditions for household registration in a large city with an urban population of 1 million to 5 million are to have a legal and stable employment for a certain number of years and a legal and stable residence in the city, and to have participated in urban social insurance for a certain number of years as prescribed by the State, provided that the requirement for the number of years of participation in urban social insurance shall not exceed five years. Among them, a large city with an urban population of 3 million to 5 million may make regulations on the scope and duration of legal and stable employment and the scope and conditions of legal and stable residence, and may also establish a points-based household registration system based on local realities.
(4) A mega city with an urban population of more than 5 million and a super mega city shall, based on the comprehensive carrying capacity of the city and the needs of economic and social development, establish and improve a points-based household registration system with the main indicators being the possession of legal and stable employment, legal and stable residence, the number of years of participation in urban social insurance, and the number of consecutive years of residence.
Article 17 State organs and their staff members shall keep confidential the personal information of the holders of the residence permit that they have learned in the course of their work.

Article 19 Whoever commits any of the following acts shall be fined by the public security organ not less than 200 yuan but not more than 1,000 yuan; if there are any illegal gains, the illegal gains shall be confiscated:
(1) Using another person's residence permit under false pretenses or using a fraudulently obtained residence permit;
(2) Purchasing, selling or using a forged or altered residence permit.
Any forged or altered residence permit and any fraudulently obtained residence permit shall be confiscated by the public security organ.

Article 21 For the first application for a residence permit, the certificate production fee shall be exempted. For replacement or reissuance of a residence permit, the certificate production fee shall be paid. No fee shall be charged for handling the endorsement procedures.
The specific fee collection measures shall be formulated by the financial department and the competent pricing department of the State Council.

Article 22 The local people's governments at or above the districted city level shall, based on factors such as the economic and social development needs and the household registration conditions of their respective administrative regions, formulate implementation measures in accordance with these Regulations.

Article 23 These Regulations shall come into force as of January 1, 2016. Residence permits already issued before the coming into force of these Regulations shall remain valid within their validity period.
